title: Domain-qualified predicates for the canonical exchange identifications and coherence laws
statement:
Use the finite-field coefficient datum and operations $S$ of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], the chosen Cartesian squares [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and their transposes [def-sf-chosen-cartesian-square-transpose]. At a positive finite quotient $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ use the canonical ordinary and compact-support maps [def-exchange-projection], their etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and the canonical etale/proetale coordinates [def-sf-finite-exchange-comparison-coordinates]. For an adic datum $d$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] use its completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], its ordered completed ordinary map [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], and its proper/open compact-support calculus [def-sf-completed-compact-support-calculus-data]. The actual completed mate and its raw rational localization are the specified operations of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange], with constructible integral and field domains as in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], [sbc-def-admissible-lattices] and [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].

Define the following propositions about these fixed maps; defining a proposition asserts none of its equations or invertibilities. Finite ordinary laws mean the identity-square equation and both pasting equations, with the canonical inverse-image and derived-direct-image compositors inserted. Finite support laws mean the analogous identity and both pasting equations for $Rp_*j_!$, the equation identifying an arbitrary chosen compactification with the prescribed one via their comparison, and the compatibility with composition of compact-support morphisms. Finite naturality is the component naturality square for the module mate. The finite module smooth predicate says, under the invertible-annihilator smooth coefficient hypothesis, smooth base change and a bounded constructible input, that the actual module mate is invertible and becomes the abelian smooth map after forgetting coefficients. The finite proetale smooth predicate says invertibility on its bounded constructible witnessed domain and equality with the etale map conjugated by the retained witness and canonical source/target comparisons. The positive-level finite-stage predicate is the conjunction of these five predicates. The finite compact identification predicate is equality of the canonical fixed-coefficient compact exchange with the proper/open map; the finite datum identification predicate says that both exchanges of $S$, transported by the specified intrinsic coefficient realizations, are those very ambient maps.

Completed ordinary laws mean naturality, the identity-square normalization and horizontal and vertical pasting on proper maps with complete inputs and finite etale-origin witnesses. Completed support laws mean the identity-square normalization, both pastings, compatibility with compactification refinements, naturality and identity/composition of refinement maps, independence and the cocycle for common-refinement comparisons, and compatibility with proper/open composition towers and their refinements, always for complete inputs with compatible origins. Completed support naturality is the component naturality equation on that same domain. Define the completed direct-image compositor to be the adjunction conjugate of the inverse completed-pullback compositor. Completed mate laws mean the completion-unit-normalized identity comparison, the identity-square mate equation, both pastings and naturality of the actual completed mate and their raw rationalized equations. Integral model identification means equality of that mate with the ambient coefficient exchange conjugated by the specified pull and push comparisons. Square naturality means equality of the mate of a pre/post-whiskered square comparison with pre/post-whiskering of this same mate. Integral normalization means its finite-reduction equation and its ordered strict-derived-limit equation.

The integral smooth predicate retains the finite-reduction origin models and imposes a common interval on all four finite output families only for its constructible landing clause. The rational smooth predicate retains a specified finite-level admissible integral lattice, equality with its transported raw exchange, independence under another admissible lattice, and its square-constructible landing implication. At an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, the common-stage smooth predicate retains the specified ambient presentation, and asserts component invertibility only for representatives admitting admissible lattices whose scalar extensions admit such lattices at every finite overfield. It includes the representative formula at every overfield and independence from the admissible integral lattice at each stage. These use exactly the domains of [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] and [sbc-thm-overline-mathbf-q-ell-coefficient-smooth-base-ch].

The rational support predicate means that the actual completed compact exchange localizes to the constructible endpoint functors, with the normalized natural isomorphism on every integral representative, and with identity, both pastings and composition equations whenever the intermediate endpoints have the stated constructible domains [thm-cbc-finite-extension]. The common-stage support predicate means that the specified compact-support exchange model exists, its descended component is represented at every dominating field by its finite-stage component conjugated by the two scalar comparisons, and this expression is independent of an isomorphism from a representing pair to the fixed input object [thm-cbc-qbar]. The at-square versions retain the chosen compactifications and all dimension and invertible-prime parameters; the global versions quantify over these same parameters. Scalar compatibility means the completed ambient exchange and its raw localization commute with the specified coefficient extension comparisons, including the lifted constructible arrow whenever both endpoints lie in the constructible domain. All common-stage categories are the raw pair categories, and no discrete non-torsion small-etale exchange or unconditional smooth constructible landing is part of these definitions.
